guideTitle: 6 Best Hardwired Motion Sensor Lights in 2026
metaTitle: Best Hardwired Motion Sensor Lights in 2026
metaDescription: Six hardwired motion sensor lights for outdoor security and indoor closets, compared on lumens, sensor range, color options and sensing modes.
introParagraphs: A hardwired motion light is the set-and-forget option. Once it is connected to your home's wiring, there are no batteries to recharge, no panels to keep in the sun and no remote to lose. It simply comes on when something moves, and it comes on at full strength every time, which is why this category is the usual choice for garages, side yards, utility closets and laundry rooms.

The six picks here split into two groups. Three are outdoor floodlights built for driveways and yards, with output from 3200 to 7500 lumens, and three are indoor ceiling fixtures meant for closets, pantries and hallways. They differ in how many heads they carry, how far the sensor reaches and whether the color temperature is selectable.

We evaluated each from product specs and buyer feedback, giving the most weight to sensor reach, light output and the number of modes. Hardwired fixtures should be installed with the power off at the breaker, and if you are unsure, a licensed electrician is the right call.

products.name: LUTEC 72W 7500LM 3-Head LED Security Light
products.description:
The LUTEC is a three-head LED security light rated at 72W and 7500 lumens in 5000K daylight white. The sensor spans a 180 degree angle and reaches up to 69 feet, and the housing carries an IP65 waterproof rating. It provides four modes: test, security, dusk to dawn and manual override.

That output and reach make it the strongest floodlight here, with enough range to cover a wide driveway or an entire side yard. Four modes mean you can use the test mode while you aim the heads at dusk, then settle on security or dusk to dawn. The manual override mode holds the light on for as long as you want, which suits working outside after dark.

Being hardwired, it needs a proper junction connection, and the three heads are heavy enough to need a solid mount. Compared with the LEPOWER at 4000 lumens, the LUTEC nearly doubles the output and adds a third head. Choose it when the area is large and you want the brightest, farthest-reaching light.
products.bestFor: Large driveways and yards that need the strongest, farthest-reaching floodlight.
pros: 7500 lumens is the brightest light in this group
Sensor reaches up to 69 ft across 180 degrees
Four modes include test and manual override
IP65 rating suits exposed outdoor walls
cons: Three heavy heads need a sturdy mounting point
Far more light than a small porch really needs

products.name: LEPOWER Hardwired LED Security Light, 40W 4000LM
products.description:
The LEPOWER is a hardwired floodlight with two LED heads rated at 40W and 4000 lumens. Its PIR sensor covers 180 degrees and reaches up to 72 feet, and it reacts to people, cars and animals. Both lamp heads and the sensor head can be angled.

A 72 foot range is actually longer than the LUTEC's 69 feet, which is useful when the light is mounted high on a garage and you want early notice down a long drive. At 4000 lumens it is bright without being overwhelming, so it suits a back door or a side yard better than a very large property. The listing does not state a weather rating the way the LUTEC does, so it is worth confirming the housing suits your exposure.

Installation follows the same pattern as any hardwired flood, with the heads aimed after mounting. In ownership it asks for nothing except an occasional wipe of the sensor lens. Next to the Onforu at 3200 lumens, the LEPOWER offers a little more output but no color temperature choice. Pick it when you want long reach at a moderate brightness.
products.bestFor: Garage fronts and long side yards that need reach without extreme brightness.
pros: 72 ft sensing range is the longest in this group
Two heads and the sensor can each be angled
Reacts to people, cars and animals alike
4000 lumens is bright without overwhelming a yard
cons: Listing gives no clear weatherproof rating
Single color tone with no temperature choice

products.name: Onforu 32W 2-Head Hardwired Motion Light, 3CCT
products.description:
The Onforu is a dual-head hardwired floodlight rated at 32W and 3200 lumens. A switch selects between 3000K warm, 4000K neutral and 6500K cool light. The sensor spans 180 degrees and reaches 19 to 72 feet, and a dusk-to-dawn mode keeps the light at 30% output through the night.

Color choice is rare in outdoor floods, and it is a real plus if you want a warm porch tone or a crisp security white from the same fixture. The 30% dusk-to-dawn level gives a gentle presence all night, then the light ramps up on motion. It is dimmer than the LUTEC and LEPOWER, which makes it better for an entry than a wide lot.

Once mounted, you choose the color at install and rarely touch it again. Against the LUTEC at 7500 lumens, the Onforu gives up brightness for flexibility. Choose it if you care how the light looks on your house, and you want a standby glow instead of full darkness.
products.bestFor: Entries and side doors where color tone and a night glow matter.
pros: Selectable 3000K, 4000K and 6500K color tones
Dusk-to-dawn mode holds 30% output through the night
Sensor range of 19 to 72 ft with 180 degree spread
Two heads aim light at two different spots
cons: 3200 lumens is the lowest of the outdoor floods
Color must be switched during install, not on the fly

products.name: Matane 12 Inch Motion Sensor LED Ceiling Light
products.description:
The Matane is a 12 inch wired flush-mount ceiling light with 2400 lumens, dimmable output and three color temperatures from 3000K to 5000K. It uses a 360 degree microwave sensor with a light sensor, and it comes with a remote control. Three modes include an AUTO mode that works only when motion is detected in the dark.

The 360 degree sensor is the main feature, since a ceiling-mounted unit can catch someone entering from any direction. The remote lets you tune brightness and color from the doorway without a stepladder. Microwave sensing can pick up movement through thin walls, so it may switch on when someone passes the other side of a partition.

As a ceiling fixture it needs a wired junction box in place of your existing light. In daily use you set the color and dimming once, and the light handles the rest. Compared with the hepside at 18W, the Matane offers a larger fixture with more lumens and a remote. Choose it for a garage, a utility room or a large closet.
products.bestFor: Garages and utility rooms that need strong all-around ceiling light.
pros: 360 degree sensing catches entry from every direction
2400 lumens lights a garage or large closet well
Remote adjusts color and brightness from the door
Light sensor keeps it off when the room is bright
cons: Microwave sensing can react to movement through thin walls
Larger 12 inch fixture is too big for a small closet

products.name: slochi 7 Inch Hardwired Motion Closet Light, 15W 1500LM
products.description:
The slochi is a 7 inch hardwired flush-mount light with 15W and 1500 lumens. It has a built-in PIR sensor with a 120 degree angle and a 3 to 4 meter range, designed for a mounting height of 2 to 3 meters. Three color temperatures and three sensor modes are offered, and three hold times let you set how long it stays on.

The compact size suits a reach-in closet, a pantry or a small hallway where a big fixture would look out of place. The ON mode bypasses the sensor, while the DAY-OUT style mode activates it only in the dark, so you get both kinds of behavior from one fixture. The 3 to 4 meter range is short, which is fine for a closet but not for a long corridor.

Holding times of different lengths mean you can tune the light so it does not drop out while you are choosing clothes. Compared with the hepside at 8.7 inches, the slochi is smaller and more compact. It is the neat answer for tight spaces.
products.bestFor: Reach-in closets, pantries and small hallways.
pros: Compact 7 inch size suits tight ceilings
Three hold times prevent drop-outs while you browse
Three color temperatures from warm to cool
ON mode lets you bypass the sensor completely
cons: 3 to 4 m range is too short for long corridors
Needs a ceiling mounting height of 2 to 3 meters

products.name: hepside 8.7 Inch Hardwired Motion Ceiling Light, 18W
products.description:
The hepside is an 8.7 inch hardwired flush-mount LED ceiling light rated at 18W. It offers three color temperatures, 3000K warm white, 4000K neutral and 6500K cool, and a PIR sensor with a 120 degree angle that detects movement within 10 to 20 feet. Three sensing modes include an ON mode that keeps the light on and bypasses the sensor.

It sits in between the compact slochi and the large Matane, which makes it a good match for a walk-in closet, laundry room or hallway. The 10 to 20 foot range is long enough to greet someone entering a mid-size room. The listing does not state a lumen number, so the 18W rating is the best guide to its brightness.

To install it, you replace an existing fixture and wire it to the junction box. After that it needs only an occasional wipe of the lens. Compared with the slochi at 1500 lumens, the hepside is slightly larger with a longer stated range. Choose it for rooms bigger than a closet but smaller than a garage.
products.bestFor: Walk-in closets, laundry rooms and mid-size hallways.
pros: Detects movement from 10 to 20 feet away
Three color temperatures suit different rooms
ON mode bypasses the sensor when you want it lit
8.7 inch size fits between compact and large fixtures
cons: Listing gives no lumen figure, only 18W
PIR arc of 120 degrees leaves side blind spots

buyingCriteria.explanation: Match the output to the space, because more is not better for a closet and less is not enough for a yard. The LUTEC delivers 7500 lumens for a wide property, the LEPOWER 4000 and the Onforu 3200 for mid-size areas, and the slochi 1500 for a small room. A single closet rarely needs more than 1500 lumens. Use higher numbers outdoors, where light disperses quickly.

How far and how wide the sensor sees decides whether the light greets you or surprises you. The LEPOWER reaches 72 feet at 180 degrees, the LUTEC reaches 69 feet, and the hepside reaches 10 to 20 feet at 120 degrees. Walking straight toward a PIR sensor triggers it later than crossing its field, so mount it where paths cross the beam. A 180 degree arc covers a wall corner, while 120 degrees covers a doorway.

An outdoor fixture needs an explicit rating, not just the word outdoor. The LUTEC lists IP65, which resists jets of water and dust. The LEPOWER does not state a rating in its listing, so verify before mounting it somewhere very exposed. Under an eave you have more latitude, but a wall facing the weather should meet at least IP65.

Color affects how the light feels and how well you see. Warm 3000K is welcoming, neutral 4000K is balanced and cool 6500K is crisp. The Onforu offers 3000K, 4000K and 6500K, and the slochi and hepside do likewise indoors. If you are not sure, choose a model with a selector so you can change it after seeing the light in place.

A hardwired light should let you set how long it stays on and when it works. The LUTEC has test, security, dusk to dawn and manual override modes, and the slochi has three hold times. Test mode helps you aim the sensor in daylight. A longer hold time keeps a closet light from dropping out while you are mid-task.

All hardwired lights need power connected through a junction box, and the work should be done with the breaker off. Heavier fixtures such as the LUTEC need a solid mounting point for three heads. Indoor ceiling lights like the Matane replace an existing fixture. If you are unsure about wiring, hire a qualified electrician.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output and coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lumens against the size of area each light is meant for. The LUTEC leads the group at 7500 lumens, followed by the LEPOWER at 4000 and the Onforu at 3200. Indoors, the Matane at 2400 lumens tops the ceiling lights, with the slochi at 1500.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sensor performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at the stated sensing range and angle. The LEPOWER reaches 72 feet and the LUTEC 69 feet across 180 degrees, while the indoor hepside covers 10 to 20 feet. The Matane stands apart with a 360 degree sensor for ceiling mounting.

howWeEvaluated.title: Flexibility of settings
howWeEvaluated.description: The number of modes, hold times and color options shaped this score. The LUTEC offers four modes, the Onforu offers three color temperatures plus dusk-to-dawn at 30%, and the slochi offers three sensor modes and three hold times.

howWeEvaluated.title: Build and weather resistance
howWeEvaluated.description: Outdoor lights were rated on explicit protection. The LUTEC lists IP65, which gave it an edge, while the LEPOWER lists no rating. For indoor fixtures we looked at size and how well each fits a small ceiling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The six picks avoid overlap. The LUTEC covers big outdoor areas, the LEPOWER and Onforu cover mid-size spots, and the Matane, hepside and slochi cover indoor rooms from large to compact.

faq.q: Which hardwired motion sensor light is best for outdoors?
faq.a: It depends on the area. The LUTEC 72W is the strongest at 7500 lumens with an IP65 rating, and it suits large properties. The LEPOWER has the longest range at 72 feet, and the Onforu adds color choices. Start with how much ground you need to cover.

faq.q: Can I install a hardwired light myself?
faq.a: It is possible if you are comfortable with household wiring, but always switch off the breaker first. Heavier fixtures like the LUTEC need a strong mounting point. If you are unsure, a licensed electrician is the safer choice. Never guess about wiring.

faq.q: Why does my light flick on during the day?
faq.a: Most hardwired lights have a daylight sensor, but some modes bypass it. Check that the mode is not set to ON or manual override. Models like the LUTEC offer a dusk-to-dawn mode that works only in the dark. Also make sure the photocell is not covered.

faq.q: Do I need a closet-specific light?
faq.a: A closet fixture should be compact and stay cool. The slochi at 7 inches and 15W suits a reach-in closet well. Keep any light away from stored fabric, and follow local code for closet fixtures. Avoid oversized lights that sit too close to shelves.

faq.q: Is a higher lumen number always better?
faq.a: No, and this is a common misconception. A closet with a 7500 lumen light would be painful, and a wide yard with 1500 lumens would be dim. The LUTEC suits large outdoor areas, while the slochi suits a closet. Choose by area, not by the biggest number.

faq.q: Why does the light shut off while I am still in the room?
faq.a: PIR sensors react best to movement across their view and may miss someone sitting still. Increase the hold time, as on the slochi, which has three settings. Mounting at the right height also helps, since the slochi is designed for 2 to 3 meters. For lights that must never drop out, use ON mode.
